items.stem: For time-ordered data, why is a random shuffle into k folds invalid?

options.text: It lets the model train on future data to predict the past
options.rationale: Correct: temporal leakage inflates the estimate.
They inflate, not reduce, the reported accuracy.

options.text: k-fold cannot be used on any data
options.rationale: k-fold is fine for non-temporal data.

items.explanation: Correct: temporal leakage inflates the estimate.

items.stem: Which TWO steps make an experiment reproducible? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Fixing random seeds and recording them
options.rationale: Correct: seeds make stochastic steps repeatable.

options.text: Logging the exact data and code version used
options.rationale: Correct: version pinning lets a run be recreated.

options.text: Reporting only the best run and discarding the rest
options.rationale: Cherry-picking hides variability and harms reproducibility.

options.text: Changing hyperparameters between runs without recording them

items.explanation: Correct: seeds make stochastic steps repeatable.

items.stem: Why report a metric with a confidence interval rather than a single number?

options.text: It communicates the uncertainty around the estimate
options.rationale: Correct: a point estimate hides run-to-run variability.
An interval does not change accuracy.

options.text: It is required to train the model
options.rationale: It is a reporting practice, not a training step.

options.text: It replaces the need for a test set
options.rationale: It does not remove the need for held-out evaluation.

items.explanation: Correct: a point estimate hides run-to-run variability.
